title: Polylogarithmic treewidth with forbidden induced minors
formal: For every integer \(t\ge 2\), does there exist an integer \(c_{t}\ge 1\) such that every n-vertex graph G with \(n\ge 2\), no clique of size t and neither Kt,t nor Wt as an induced minor satisfies \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\le c_{t}(\log _{2} n)^{c_{t}}\)?
why: Would yield a substantially stronger structural bound for graphs excluding two induced-minor patterns and large cliques. Polylogarithmic treewidth supports quasipolynomial algorithms for many problems whose dependence on treewidth is exponential, making the quantitative improvement algorithmically significant.
status_note: Original question and the unambiguous March 2026 formulation checked, with searches through 11 September 2026. The subpolynomial and coarse-decomposition results do not resolve the stated polylogarithmic treewidth target. Preprint theorem statements were matched to the model; proofs were not independently verified.

sentences: Treewidth measures the largest bag needed to organize a graph in a tree decomposition.
The question concerns graphs with no large clique and with neither a fixed complete bipartite graph nor a fixed wall as an induced minor.
It asks whether their treewidth is bounded by a fixed power of the logarithm of their number of vertices.
A March 2026 preprint proves a subpolynomial bound but still states the polylogarithmic target as a conjecture.
The stronger bound would improve the structural and algorithmic understanding of these induced-minor-free graph classes.

references.title: Solving Problems on Graphs: From Structure to Algorithms

definitions: All graphs are finite, undirected and simple. Write \(n=|V(G)|\) and take logarithms in base two. An induced subgraph \(G[S]\) retains precisely all edges of G whose endpoints are in S. Kt is the complete graph on t vertices; Kt,t is the complete bipartite graph with two independent sets of t vertices and every edge between the sets. A tree decomposition consists of a finite tree T and bags \(Bx\subseteq V(G)\), one per node x of T, such that every vertex occurs in a bag, both endpoints of every edge occur together in some bag, and the bags containing any fixed vertex form a connected subtree of T. Its width is maxx |\(Bx|- 1\). Treewidth \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\) is the minimum width of such a decomposition. For a concrete wall convention, construct Wt from vertices \((i,j), 0\le i\le t\) and \(0\le j\le 2t+1\): include all horizontal edges \((i,j)(i,j+1)\), and vertical edges \((i,j)(i+1,j)\) exactly when \(i+j\) is even, then repeatedly delete vertices of degree at most one until none remain. This is a fixed elementary hexagonal-wall family. Standard wall-size conventions differ by a fixed reindexing; since the source statement quantifies over every fixed t and allows its constants to depend arbitrarily on t, this indexing does not change the family-level claim. An induced minor is obtained by deleting vertices and contracting edges, with loops discarded and parallel edges merged, but without arbitrary edge deletions. Equivalently, its vertices can be represented by pairwise disjoint nonempty connected branch sets in G, with an edge between two branch sets exactly when their corresponding vertices are adjacent in the induced minor. The clique exclusion is an ordinary clique/induced-subgraph condition; the exclusions of Kt,t and Wt are induced-minor conditions. There is no bound on maximum degree. The constant \(c_{t}\) and the exponent \(c_{t}\) may depend on t, but not on n or G. Allowing separate constants for the multiplier and exponent is equivalent by increasing \(c_{t}\), since \(\log _{2} n\ge 1\). The statement is structural existence of tree decompositions and requests no algorithm for finding them. Restricting to \(t,n\ge 2\) removes only trivial small or undefined-log cases.
answer_criterion: Prove the displayed bound for every t with constants depending only on t, or refute it by finding one fixed t for which, for every integer \(c\ge 1\), there is an admitted graph G with \(\operatorname{tw}(G)>c(\log _{2} |V(G)|)^{c}\). A subpolynomial upper bound or a bound on independence number inside bags does not establish the requested polylogarithmic bound on bag size.

context_blocks.title: Treewidth measures the size of the pieces
context_blocks.text: A tree decomposition organizes overlapping vertex sets along a tree. Vertices may appear in several bags, but their occurrences must remain connected. A path has treewidth one, whereas a complete graph on n vertices has treewidth \(n- 1\). Small bags allow many graph problems to be processed through their interactions along the decomposition.

context_blocks.title: Which large structures are excluded
context_blocks.text: The question removes large cliques and two specific induced-minor patterns: a complete bipartite graph and a hexagonal wall. Induced minors permit edge contractions but preserve the presence of edges between surviving branch sets. This makes their exclusion different from forbidding an ordinary graph minor, where arbitrary edges may also be deleted.

context_blocks.title: A polylogarithmic target
context_blocks.text: For each fixed t, the requested bound is a constant times a fixed power of log n. The power can grow with t. The statement does not ask for a constant treewidth bound and does not impose the maximum-degree restriction of the separate logarithmic-degree question.

context_blocks.title: Subpolynomial progress leaves a gap
context_blocks.text: The March 2026 version of Chudnovsky and coauthors’ preprint states \(\operatorname{tw}(G)\le 2^{a_{t}(\log _{2} n)^{1- \varepsilon _{t}}}\) for constants \(a_{t}\) and \(\varepsilon _{t}>0\) under these same exclusions. It states the polylogarithmic bound separately as Conjecture 1.1. The reported upper bound is subpolynomial in n, but does not establish that conjecture.

context_blocks.title: Other bag measures have different meanings
context_blocks.text: The May 2026 coarse-decomposition preprint bounds how many vertices in a bag can be far apart in the original graph. A bag can contain many nearby vertices while that number remains small. Such bounds are not bounds on the number of vertices in the bag, which is what treewidth counts.
